study.comparator: glibenclamide 5 mg three times daily, both arms on metformin
study.notes: STUDY: multicentre randomised single blind controlled trial (Italy, Pavia and seven other centres) in type 2 diabetes uncontrolled on metformin: exenatide 5 ug twice daily titrated after 1 month to 10 ug twice daily (dose_mg 0.01 per injection) vs glibenclamide 2.5 mg three times daily titrated to 5 mg three times daily, 12 months (52 weeks entered); 128 randomised (63 exenatide, 65 glibenclamide, Table 1), 116 completed, 59 and 57 at 12 months (Tables 2 and 3 Number row), the 12 withdrawals listed by reason and arm; Table 1 gives baseline and Tables 2 and 3 give 3, 6, 9 and 12 month mean plus or minus SD per arm (route arm_change_imputed_r, correlation 0.5; the asterisks and daggers are within arm and between arm tests without values, not used); body weight, glycaemic control, beta cell function, insulin resistance and inflammatory state are the stated aims (prespecified TRUE); pct_weight_change from the Table 1 and Table 2 means in the exenatide arm, 82.0 to 74.0 kg, minus 8.0 kg equals minus 9.8 percent (glibenclamide 82.4 to 86.7 kg, plus 5.2 percent; no contrast printed); authors certify no financial involvement, no funding statement (industry_funded FALSE); rob_overall some_concerns

rows.notes: Table 1 baseline and Tables 2 and 3 at 12 months: HbA1c percent per arm; p below 0.001 vs baseline in both arms, no between arm difference stated
Table 1 baseline and Tables 2 and 3 at 12 months: fasting plasma glucose mg/dL per arm
Table 1 baseline and Tables 2 and 3 at 12 months: fasting plasma insulin uU/mL per arm; marked p below 0.01 vs baseline and vs glibenclamide at 12 months
Table 1 baseline and Tables 2 and 3 at 12 months: HOMA-IR index per arm; marked p below 0.01 vs baseline and vs glibenclamide at 12 months
Table 1 baseline and Tables 2 and 3 at 12 months: HOMA-beta index per arm; marked p below 0.01 vs baseline and p below 0.05 vs glibenclamide at 12 months
Table 1 baseline and Tables 2 and 3 at 12 months: hs-CRP mg/L per arm (latex enhanced immunonephelometry); marked p below 0.001 vs baseline and p below 0.05 vs glibenclamide at 12 months

json.design: multicentre randomised single blind controlled trial, exenatide twice daily vs glibenclamide on metformin, type 2 diabetes, 128 randomised, 116 completed (59 and 57), 12 months
json.reason: full text group (institutional route); six inventory markers with baseline (Table 1) and 12 month (Tables 2 and 3) mean and SD per arm by the imputed change route; a different trial from Derosa 2011 exenatide vs glimepiride (group 272) and from the pre systematic Derosa 2012
other_markers: proinsulin and proinsulin to insulin ratio

rob.justification: randomised without a described sequence or concealment, balanced baseline (D1 some concerns); single blind with titrated comparator (D2 some concerns); 12 of 128 withdrew with reasons by arm, 59 and 57 analysed at 12 months (D3 low); laboratory outcomes (D4 low); no registration cited, aims list the marker set (D5 some concerns)

doubts: the 12 month means come from the completers tabulated at each visit (Number row), not an intention to treat set
the glibenclamide arm gained 4.3 kg while the exenatide arm lost 8.0 kg, so the HOMA-IR and hsCRP contrasts reflect opposite weight trajectories
